title: Durable immunity at the respiratory surface that stops transmission

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a safe vaccine that establishes lasting protection where a respiratory virus first encounters the body: the airway surface. It would prevent infection and onward transmission, including after antigenic changes that help the targeted virus evade earlier immunity. The biological strategy is to establish local defenses such as secretory IgA antibodies and tissue-resident memory cells that can restrict infection at its entry site. The supplied review describes these mechanisms and their promise, but does not establish the complete human capability.

The intended outcome combines several distinct achievements: protection at respiratory surfaces, persistence over time, effectiveness against drifted strains, prevention of infection, and prevention of onward spread. These cannot be treated as interchangeable. A strong circulating antibody response, a local immune response, protection against severe disease, and reduced transmission each answer different questions. The innovation requires convincing evidence for the combined outcome, rather than inference from any one immune measurement.

significance.text: Systemically administered respiratory vaccines can protect against severe disease while incompletely preventing early viral replication, infection, and onward spread. Durable protection at respiratory entry sites would add a major capability: preventing infections that existing disease protection still permits. Fewer infections and less transmission from vaccinated people would be direct consequences of achieving the proposed outcome. This does not imply that injected vaccines never reduce infection or transmission.

At population scale, reducing transmission can lower the effective reproductive number and slow outbreak growth. If effectiveness, duration, and vaccine coverage were sufficient under prevailing transmission conditions, the innovation could help interrupt epidemics caused by the targeted virus. Interruption would remain conditional: a successful individual-level trial would not itself guarantee adequate uptake, equitable access, or transmission below replacement in every setting.

Scope limit and synthesis: success against one respiratory virus and an antigenically drifted strain would establish an important capability for that tested setting, not a solution for every respiratory RNA virus. Protection at the airway surface and antigenic breadth are separate dimensions. A mucosal vaccine could recognize only a narrow range of strains, while broad recognition measured in blood would still require separate evidence of protection at respiratory surfaces. The supplied evidence does not establish the original measles analogy or a general rule that short incubation defines the unresolved class.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability is maintaining effective local protection long enough to prevent both infection and transmission despite viral drift. Systemic vaccination often produces limited local mucosal responses even when circulating responses are strong. Local IgA and resident immune cells can be induced, but the supplied review identifies their decay and the mechanisms governing their persistence as continuing problems. The evidence supports this limitation; it does not establish a universal rule that systemic immunity always arrives at mucosal sites too late.

Engineering barriers include reliable mucosal delivery, durable induction of the relevant local defenses, and a safety profile suitable for vaccination of healthy people. Antigenic drift adds a separate biological barrier: immunity must retain useful recognition as the targeted virus changes. Improving one component does not automatically solve the others, so delivery, persistence, cross-strain protection, and safety must be evaluated together.

Measurement is also a missing capability. The review identifies unresolved standardized correlates and sampling approaches, while distinguishing protection against transmission, severe disease, and infection. A useful human correlate for this innovation must predict the specified infection or transmission outcome under defined conditions. Antibody levels or resident-cell measurements alone cannot establish that prediction, and the absence of an agreed standardized correlate does not mean every possible human predictor has been ruled out.

current_state.text: Beeton and Case's 2026 review, dated 23 July 2026 in the research notes, reports five mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccines approved for human use at the time of publication. Existing human mucosal vaccines therefore need to be distinguished from the stronger capability proposed here. The supplied review identifies continuing challenges in durability, antigenic drift, delivery, and standardized correlates; the evidence provided does not establish that an approved product meets the combined multi-season, drift-resistant infection and transmission endpoints.

The same review reports an animal experiment in which a single intranasal dose of a viral-vectored SARS-CoV-2 vaccine given to donor hamsters prevented subsequent transmission to vaccinated and unvaccinated recipient animals. This is a concrete partial demonstration of the transmission goal. It is review-level evidence for an animal result, rather than an independently inspected primary experiment, and does not establish multi-season protection, drift resistance, or equivalent outcomes in humans.

Unverified research leads retained for context: the research notes attribute a discussion of secretory IgA and resident memory to Tang and colleagues, with an electronic publication date of 15 April 2026. They also describe a 2025 macaque study in which an intranasal adenovirus boost after mRNA immunization produced strong mucosal responses and near-absent virus after an Omicron-lineage challenge, and a mouse study dated 19 February 2026 reporting protection against several respiratory challenges for at least three months through a TLR-ligand nasal formulation and trained macrophages. No supplied source artifact verifies these descriptions, dates, or quantitative claims. They remain unresolved leads, not established demonstrations in this record. If verified, the mouse result would represent an antigen-nonspecific mechanism distinct from antigen-specific vaccine memory; neither animal description by itself establishes human transmission blockade.

Evidence boundary: the supplied review assessment describes the Beeton and Case artifact as identity-verified, full text, untruncated, and without reported extraction issues. The limitations concern the other unsupplied source texts and the absence of a freshness search, rather than reported truncation of that review. The supplied evidence does not establish a qualifying human product, but it also cannot establish an exhaustive worldwide absence through 1 November 2026 because the freshness record is empty. Missing evidence for an example is not proof that the example is false.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: a controlled human trial should show prevention of documented infection and a separately measured reduction in onward transmission for a defined respiratory RNA virus, including an antigenically drifted strain, with protection assessed across more than one season. The protocol should specify how large and persistent the effects must be to count as success. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established consensus standards. A single mouse challenge showing no detectable infection would not satisfy them.
completion_criteria.label: Multiseason human infection prevention and transmission reduction including drifted strains

completion_criteria.text: Proposed measurement requirements: prespecify infection ascertainment, testing frequency, exposure definitions, strain identification, and how transmission from vaccinated participants to contacts will be attributed. Infection prevention and transmission prevention should be reported separately, including transmission from breakthrough infections where measurable. Analyses should state uncertainty and the limits of detection; observing no infections in a finite sample cannot prove a literal inability to become infected.
completion_criteria.label: Prespecified ascertainment and separate infection and transmission estimates with uncertainty

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: confirm the findings in independent cohorts or trials, disclose prior infection and vaccination histories, and test whether protection persists under the intended dosing schedule and delivery conditions. Define acceptable adverse-event rates and severity in advance for the intended healthy population. Report any dependence on repeated boosting, particular exposure levels, age groups, or strains. These boundaries determine the demonstrated practical capability rather than serving as reasons to discard a useful but limited result.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication with prespecified safety criteria and reported practical boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed correlate validation: any immune measurement used to predict success should be prospectively validated against the specified human infection and transmission endpoints, with standardized sampling and independent confirmation. A correlate emerging from VIR-09 could contribute if it predicts those outcomes. Testing several seasons and strains would establish demonstrated duration and breadth within those observations, not permanent immunity or universal protection against future variants.
completion_criteria.label: Prospectively validated immune correlates predict human infection and transmission outcomes

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: VIR-04, protective immunity covering a viral family including future variants and unseen relatives, concerns the breadth of recognition. VIR-05 concerns the location, persistence, and transmission consequences of immunity. Drift resistance creates overlap, but neither capability subsumes the other. VIR-09, a mechanistic correlate predicting human protection from a new virus, could supply a measurement framework for VIR-05 only if validated for its particular infection and transmission outcomes. Only roster titles were supplied for these entries, so their detailed requirements and exact interfaces cannot be verified.

Roster-based synthesis: VIR-01 could help predict changes in infectivity, transmission, or escape and thereby inform strain selection and testing, while VIR-08 could reveal functions of unfamiliar viral genes. Both concern knowledge that might guide vaccine development; neither title specifies durable airway protection. VIR-07 overlaps at the level of viral delivery technology, but targeting human cells, permitting repeat administration, and carrying large genes are different capabilities from establishing lasting respiratory immunity.

Roster-based synthesis: VIR-02 addresses empiric medicines for severe acute viral disease, whereas VIR-05 aims to prevent respiratory infection and spread. VIR-03 targets elimination or permanent silencing of persistent viral genomes; VIR-10 targets chronic suppression through a conditionally replicating interfering particle; and VIR-11 targets an interruptible causal chain between persistent infection and chronic disease. These address different stages or consequences of infection. VIR-06 concerns reliable bacteriophage treatment of bacterial disease and is distinct in both its therapeutic target and its completion outcome. These relationships are inferred from the supplied titles and preserve each entry as a separate concept.

unresolved_issues: The supplied materials do not determine whether any human product met the combined criteria by 1 November 2026; the freshness record is empty.

The Tang attribution, 2025 macaque challenge result, and February 2026 trained-macrophage mouse result, including its reported duration of at least three months, remain unverified because their source texts were not supplied.

The review's recommendation to replace the unverified animal examples was adopted for the demonstrated-evidence narrative, but the examples were also preserved as qualified research leads to retain explanatory detail without inventing verification.

The five reported human vaccine approvals are a review-time count; the supplied assessment does not establish their current regulatory status, jurisdiction-specific availability, or performance against the combined proposed endpoints.

The proposed human demonstration still requires numerical efficacy thresholds, a defined duration and booster schedule, exposure and drift definitions, transmission-attribution methods, and explicit acceptable safety limits.
The mechanisms that sustain local protection and the immune measurements that reliably predict human transmission prevention remain open.
Precise overlap with VIR-04 and VIR-09 cannot be established from roster titles alone.

brief.title: Lasting vaccine protection that stops respiratory spread
possible: People could avoid catching a respiratory virus and passing it to others, with vaccine protection that lasts across seasons even as the virus changes. The vaccine would build lasting immune defenses at the airway surface, where infection begins.
why: Vaccines that prevent severe illness can still leave room for infection and spread. Preventing those infections would protect vaccinated people and reduce the virus they pass to others.
Less transmission could slow outbreak growth. With enough people protected for long enough, it could help interrupt epidemics caused by the targeted virus.

sources.who: Komal Beeton and James Brett Case
sources.showed: Their review describes how vaccines delivered to airway surfaces build local immune defenses. It identifies fading protection, safe delivery and reliable measurements as continuing challenges.
sources.quote: However, they often failed to consistently elicit robust immunity at mucosal sites.
sources.cited_for: The review explains why protection at airway surfaces matters and what limits its durability.
sources.not_established: It does not demonstrate lasting human protection against both infection and transmission as the virus changes.

sources.who: Oscar Bladh, Charlotte Thålin and collaborators
sources.showed: In a human observational study, higher nasal IgA, an antibody in airway secretions, was associated with a lower risk of flu infection.
sources.quote: baseline nasal H1-specific IgA above median was associated with reduced H1N1 infection risk
sources.cited_for: Nasal antibody levels could help predict protection against infection.
sources.not_established: The association does not prove that raising nasal IgA with a vaccine prevents infection or onward transmission.

sources.showed: A nasal vaccine made from weakened coronavirus outperformed an injected vaccine at limiting transmission in hamsters, including after exposure to an Omicron variant.
sources.quote: Our findings demonstrate that the live-attenuated vaccine (LAV) sCPD9-ΔFCS significantly outperformed the mRNA vaccine in preventing virus transmission in both scenarios.
sources.cited_for: Animal experiments demonstrate that a nasal vaccine can limit infection and onward spread.
sources.not_established: Hamster results do not establish lasting protection or equivalent transmission prevention in humans.

sources.who: The researchers conducting clinical trial NCT05886790
sources.showed: A randomized human trial compared inhaled and injected coronavirus boosters. Inhaled vaccines caused fewer reported adverse reactions, and researchers measured immune responses over time.
sources.quote: No serious adverse events were recorded.
sources.cited_for: The trial supports the feasibility of inhaled vaccination and provides human safety and immune-response data.
sources.not_established: It does not establish sustained prevention of infection and transmission, or exclude rare harms.

shown: Adler and colleagues demonstrated reduced coronavirus transmission in hamsters given a nasal vaccine. In humans, Bladh and colleagues linked higher nasal antibody levels to lower flu infection risk. Human trials have also measured responses to inhaled vaccines.
missing: A human demonstration of protection against infection and onward spread across seasons, including a changed strain.
Reliable delivery that sustains airway defenses with safety suitable for healthy people.
Standardized immune measurements that reliably predict human infection and transmission outcomes.

milestones.label: Lasting human protection against infection and spread
milestones.explanation: A controlled human trial would have to show infection prevention and reduced onward spread across seasons, including a changed strain. This would demonstrate the combined capability.

milestones.label: Separate, reliable estimates of infection and transmission
milestones.explanation: Trials would have to define testing, exposure, strain identification and transmission attribution in advance, then report separate estimates with uncertainty. This would distinguish protection from missed infections.

milestones.label: Independent confirmation with clear safety and practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent studies would have to confirm protection under intended dosing and delivery, with prior immunity disclosed and safety criteria set beforehand. Reported limits would establish whom the vaccine protects and under what conditions.

milestones.label: Immune measurements that predict human protection
milestones.explanation: Standardized immune measurements would have to predict later human infection and transmission outcomes, with independent confirmation. This would establish reliable indicators of protection.

uncertain: The mechanisms that keep airway immune defenses active over time remain unclear.
Success thresholds for protection, duration, viral change and acceptable harms still need definition.
Protection against a tested virus and changed strain would not establish protection against every respiratory virus or future variant.

page.title: Transmission-blocking mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccines
page.definition: A vaccine establishes immunity in the respiratory mucosa, the airway lining, that reduces SARS-CoV-2 infection and onward spread for at least 12 months. Protection includes tested antigenically drifted variants, whose viral targets recognized by immunity differ from the vaccine strain.

goal.need: In a US household study conducted from 1 January 2024 to 31 January 2025, 476 of 763 contacts of 362 infected participants tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 during 10-day follow-up. Vaccination of the infected participant within 6 months was associated with lower transmission risk, adjusted relative risk 0.57 (95% CI 0.35–0.93). The contacts’ own vaccination status was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in infection risk.

figures.caption: Household infection risk by time since the infected participant’s last COVID-19 vaccination.
figures.note: Unadjusted risks from an observational study; these groups do not establish a causal waning curve.

statements.body: NIAID, CEPI, the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, BARDA and Wellcome, joint mucosal-vaccine workshop report
statements.quote: A priority goal for next-generation COVID-19 vaccines is to reduce infection with and transmission of SARS-CoV-2 via the respiratory route

statements.body: World Health Organization, COVID-19 vaccine target product profile
statements.quote: vaccines with efficacy against transmission are preferred.
statements.context: This is an additional preference in the booster-dose efficacy profile; its numerical efficacy thresholds address symptomatic or severe disease.

completion.title: One mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine demonstrates infection and transmission protection lasting at least 12 months.
completion.criterion: One respiratory mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine regimen induces measurable airway immunity and demonstrates reduced laboratory-confirmed infection and at least 90% lower onward transmission/infectivity, with reduced shedding, over at least 12 months in controlled human studies. Protection includes a tested antigenically drifted variant. Infection in vaccine recipients and transmission to contacts are measured separately. Safety supports regulatory authorization in the tested population. BARDA supplies the numerical transmission and duration targets; their combination with direct clinical outcomes is an Atlas synthesis.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of BARDA’s published targets and the joint NIAID–CEPI workshop goal.
completion.basis: WHO’s 2022 profile, BARDA’s 2024 profile, the joint NIAID–CEPI workshop report and registered mucosal vaccine trial endpoints were searched. No integrated test covering human infection, directly measured transmission, duration and antigenic drift was found. BARDA’s phase 2b design uses asymptomatic PCR-positive infection as a transmission surrogate; meeting that endpoint alone would leave direct transmission untested.

milestones.title: A mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine protects animals and reduces viral replication in airway tissues.
milestones.criterion: BARDA’s nonclinical target requires protective immunity, cross-protection against circulating or emerging strains, and reduced airway-tissue replication. Adler and colleagues reported on 2 February 2024 that sCPD9-ΔFCS-vaccinated hamster contacts had no detectable viral antigen in nasal epithelium six days after exposure to B.1 or BA.5; there were 6 vaccinated contacts per variant group. This is animal evidence.
milestones.set_by: BARDA investigators, Project NextGen target product profile, Table 1, nonclinical safety and efficacy row; the criterion appears only in a table.

milestones.title: FDA permits a human trial of a respiratory mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine.
milestones.criterion: A US trial can proceed when its Investigational New Drug application takes effect: 30 days after FDA receipt without a clinical hold, or upon earlier FDA permission; institutional review-board approval is also required. The MPV/S-2P nasal-vaccine consent form, approved on 12 June 2024, states that FDA permits the study. Its planned enrollment was approximately 60 adults; this is trial permission, not a safety or efficacy finding.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, 21 CFR 312.40, explained in Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: An inhaled SARS-CoV-2 booster gives a day-28 serum antibody titre ratio with 95% CI lower bound >1.
milestones.criterion: In protocol NCT05886790, the lower bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval for the day-28 serum XBB.1.5 neutralizing-antibody geometric mean titre ratio, bivalent inhaled Ad5-CoV5T versus ancestral inhaled Ad5-nCoV, must exceed 1. The randomized study enrolled 450 adults, 150 per group across three groups. Published on 7 August 2025, the ratio was 1.48 (95% CI 1.12–1.97); no serious adverse events were recorded over 6 months. This endpoint establishes serum immunogenicity.
milestones.set_by: Investigators of registered protocol NCT05886790, statistical analysis and primary hypothesis in Wu and colleagues.

milestones.title: A nasal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine rejects efficacy ≤30% against symptomatic infection in a phase 3 trial.
milestones.criterion: Protocol ChiCTR2100051391 requires rejection of vaccine efficacy ≤30% at two-sided p<0.05 for RT-PCR-confirmed symptomatic infection beginning 15 days after dose 2, versus placebo. The dNS1-RBD study randomized 31,038 adults from 16 December 2021 to 31 May 2022; 25,742 entered the per-protocol efficacy analysis. Efficacy was 28.2% (95% CI 3.4–46.6), with median follow-up of 161 days. This vaccine did not meet the protocol’s success criterion.
milestones.set_by: Investigators of registered phase 3 protocol ChiCTR2100051391; this threshold was specified for dNS1-RBD.
milestones.threshold_quote: The success criterion required rejection of the null hypothesis (a vaccine efficacy of ≤30%)

milestones.title: A mucosal SARS-CoV-2 vaccine reduces transmission/infectivity by ≥50% over at least 12 months.
milestones.criterion: Meet BARDA’s lower transmission target: ≥50% reduction in transmission/infectivity and reduced shedding over ≥12 months. Its phase 2b design measures asymptomatic PCR-positive infection as a surrogate. Vaxart’s 6 July 2026 release reported 12-month sentinel results in 201 oral-vaccine and 199 mRNA-vaccine recipients: 33 versus 30 symptomatic cases. That cohort was not powered for comparative efficacy and did not establish this transmission target. These company results were not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: BARDA investigators, Project NextGen target product profile, Table 1, transmission row, Next-Generation Threshold Criteria; the criterion appears only in a table.

not_found: No published human study meeting the combined completion test was located.
No explicit comparator, confidence-bound requirement or numerical definition of antigenic drift was found in BARDA’s transmission row.
The NIH announcement of the MPV/S-2P trial returned HTTP 403; the registered trial’s consent form was accessible.

results.finding: sCPD9-∆FCS-vaccinated hamster contacts had no detectable nasal epithelial antigen; n=6 per variant.
results.detail: The study tested exposure to both B.1 and BA.5 and also found evidence of reduced viral replication and protection against pneumonia.
results.quote: While SARS-CoV-2-positive cells were absent in nasal respiratory and olfactory epithelium of sCPD9-∆FCS-vaccinated contacts, antigen was detected in abundance in mRNA- and mock-vaccinated animals

results.finding: All 6 naive contacts of sCPD9-∆FCS-vaccinated, B.1-infected hamsters remained negative for viral RNA.
results.detail: This is short-term animal evidence of reduced onward transmission. The study did not investigate durability, so it does not establish the 12-month target.
results.quote: In contrast, contacts of sCPD9-∆FCS-vaccinated and B.1-infected animals remained negative for SARS-CoV-2 sgRNA and gRNA in the upper and lower airways, with no replicating virus detected in the lower airways.

results.finding: In 450 randomized adults, the day-28 XBB.1.5 neutralizing-antibody titre ratio was 1.48 for inhaled Ad5-CoV5T versus Ad5-nCoV.
results.detail: There were 150 participants per group. The 95% confidence interval was 1.12–1.97, with a lower bound above 1. This establishes serum immunogenicity, not transmission protection.

results.finding: In the phase 3 dNS1-RBD trial, vaccine efficacy against symptomatic infection was 28.2% among 25,742 per-protocol participants.
results.detail: The 95% CI was 3.4–46.6%. The trial did not reject efficacy of 30% or less and did not meet its predefined success criterion. Median follow-up was 161 days.
results.quote: The incidence of confirmed symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection caused by omicron variants regardless of immunisation history was 1·6% in the vaccine group and 2·3% in the placebo group, resulting in an overall vaccine efficacy of 28·2% (95% CI 3·4–46·6), with a median follow-up duration of 161 days.
